note: In-world reasoning tools. Residents may use any of the 108 patterns by id; scene lists are only starting candidates. patterns.json is unchanged.

QM037.play: Agree with the fewest builders needed who bids on which tender, so you stop undercutting each other.

QM040.play: Propose taking turns: this tender is yours, the next is mine.

QM025.play: Announce a confident price first and watch who backs off.

QM027.play: Talk in price ranges, not one number, to keep rivals guessing.

QM045.play: Write every pact promise down so breaking it is visible.

QM034.play: Offer a subcontract: share the work and the pay with a complementary builder.

QM061.play: Notice a rival's claimed rush or 'final offer' may be invented.

QM106.play: Look for bids that are oddly close together or wins that rotate: a hidden pact.

material_trade.label: Selling a skill output as building material

QM026.play: Tie every price cut to something you get back.

QM028.play: Split the deal: part now, part on delivery.

QM029.play: Mention other buyers or sellers so the other side knows you can walk away.

QM030.play: Bargain price, timing and risk separately.

QM033.play: Offer two or three options instead of one take-it-or-leave-it price.

QM062.play: Check whether the 'only one left' scarcity is real.

QM014.play: Start with a small trade to test the other side.

council_vote.label: Council votes: lobbying, vote swaps, coalitions, bans

QM037.play: Count heads: build the smallest group that reaches a majority.

QM038.play: Link two camps that distrust each other but want compatible things.

QM041.play: Protect a minority so they join you instead of blocking.

QM043.play: Announce what you will push for before the vote.

QM101.play: Say openly how the change pays you (or demand others do).

QM026.play: Trade votes: my yes on yours for your yes on mine.

QM066.play: A favour or payment does not oblige a vote; notice reciprocity pressure.

QM064.play: A majority alone does not prove a change is good for you.

QM072.play: An earlier stance does not bind you when the facts change.

capability_proposal.label: Capability proposals (proposer earns standing and a royalty per use)

QM103.play: Pitch it as a small pilot first.

QM104.play: Offer an automatic sunset so doubters can agree.

QM108.play: Argue that a useless or risky capability should be retired.

QM019.play: Show who gains and who loses from the capability.

QM101.play: Disclose your royalty interest, or point out someone else's.

QM037.play: Line up the residents who gain before the vote.

QM014.play: Make a small promise and keep it to earn trust.

QM015.play: Compare what someone says with what they did before.

QM017.play: Put the key promise on record.

QM079.play: Admit a specific harm and offer a checkable repair.

QM083.play: If it was a misunderstanding, roll back to before the conflict.

verification.label: Checking a claim (costs time; costs a fee to the speaker if the claim was true)

QM013.play: Check identity, fact and promise separately.

QM016.play: Use more than one source before believing it.

QM022.play: Rate the claim: rumour, observation, record or proof.

QM023.play: Check the speaker really has what they claim (skill, contract, offer).

QM050.play: Treat an unchecked claim as a rumour.

QM056.play: Prefer claims that could be proven false.

QM085.play: Walk away when your red line is hit.

QM087.play: Cap the time; no progress means review.

QM090.play: List what is still owed before leaving.

QM092.play: Leave quietly when no conflict is needed.

QM096.play: A failed deal need not make an enemy.
